one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I checked each verifier check against the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 4 hold. Check 1 tests only that clamp is exported and that its results stay limited to lo..hi, including edge cases those words cover. Check 2 tests only that lo>hi throws a RangeError. Check 4 tests only that `npm test` exits 0. Check 3 breaks the rule. Its FAIL condition rests on the regex `'\\b'+n+'\\s*\\('`, which fails any exported function whose name is not followed by an opening parenthesis somewhere in README.md. The line "README.md documents every function math.js exports" does not require that form. A README could document `clamp` fully under a heading like "clamp" or "`clamp` — returns…" and still fail with "MISSING". That is a wording/format rule inside a FAIL condition when it belongs under Advisory. The output does have an Advisory section, but this stricter test is not in it.

runs-as-written.why: Checks 1, 2 and 4 run as written. Check 3 breaks. Its node -e script is in double quotes, so bash turns `\\b` into `\b`, `\\s` into `\s` and `\\(` into `\(`. Node then gets `new RegExp('\b'+n+'\s*\(')`. In a JS string, '\b' is a backspace character, '\s' is a plain 's' and '\(' is a plain '('. The pattern ends in an unclosed '(', so new RegExp throws a SyntaxError (unterminated group) before anything prints. The builder brief's steps (edit math.js, README.md and test/math.test.js, then run `npm test`) are fine. Because one verifier command fails as written, the criterion is not met.

catches-traps.why:
I checked all three must_catch items, and the briefs handle each one.

1. The builder brief says subtract is "NOT documented there yet". Step 2 has the builder add a "### subtract(a, b)" subsection alongside clamp, so item 1 is covered.

2. Check 3 gets the exported names from math.js at the PR head and says this "should include add, subtract, multiply and clamp". It FAILs if "any exported function prints `MISSING`", and it also requires reading the README to confirm each function is described. The advisory says the PR must document subtract. So item 2 is covered.

3. Check 2 calls clamp with lo greater than hi three times and tests `e instanceof RangeError`. It prints `OTHER` for any other error and FAILs on that, so item 3 is covered.

One flaw outside this criterion: shell and JavaScript escaping will likely garble Check 3's regex (`'\\b'` ends up as a backspace character). The manual README reading and the stated FAIL condition still catch a missing subtract.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both must_not items against the verifier brief. Item 1: Check 3 lists every exported function by name and fails on any `MISSING`. Its PASS line says it "should include add, subtract, multiply and clamp", and the advisory notes that "subtract was undocumented before this change". A README that covers clamp but not subtract cannot pass. Item 2: Check 1 compares exact return values, which only tests clamp's clamping behaviour. Check 2 only needs `instanceof RangeError` and does not require any message. Check 3 needs a mention plus a description of each function, with no required layout. The heading style, RangeError mention and tests are all labelled "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)". Check 4 only needs a zero exit status. One problem outside this criterion: Check 3's regex escapes probably break inside double quotes in the shell, so the command may error. That would make the check unreliable but not stricter than line 3.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief's steps with the verifier's checks. Builder step 3 gives the exact input/output pairs the verifier uses as its probe: "clamp(50, 0, 100) === 50", "clamp(-5, 0, 100) === 0", "clamp(140, 0, 100) === 100", "clamp(0, 0, 100) === 0", "clamp(100, 0, 100) === 100", "clamp(7, 3, 3) === 3" and "clamp(1, 10, 0)" throwing a RangeError. Verifier check 1 runs c(50,0,100), c(-5,0,100), c(140,0,100), c(0,0,100), c(100,0,100) and c(7,3,3), and check 2 runs [1,10,0]. The criterion allows telling the builder to write its own tests, but not giving it a set of inputs with expected outputs that also appears in the verifier brief. Step 2's rule that every exported name needs its own heading is also similar to check 3's condition. The builder brief leaks the checker's methods.
